column4: The Holy Spirit is not a new spirit but is of God and has been with God since the very beginning. In Genesis 1:2 the Spirit of God is hovering on the waters during creation. In Nehemiah 9:20, the scriptures say that it was the Spirit who instructed the people in the wilderness. It was by this same Holy Spirit that God anointed the kings, judges, and prophets in the Old Testament. In Joel 2:28-29 the Spirit is promised to be poured out on all mankind. It was by this same Holy Spirit that God raised Jesus from the dead, and now dwells in us (Romans 8:11). There is only one Holy Spirit, and He has always been the same. How He works with people has looked different at different times, but His heart has never changed.
column5: The Holy Spirit is not a new spirit but is God's Spirit and has been with God from the beginning. In Genesis 1:2 the Spirit of God was hovering over the waters during creation. In Nehemiah 9:20, the Word says that it was the Spirit who taught the people in the wilderness. Through this same Holy Spirit God anointed kings, judges, and prophets in the Old Testament. In Joel 2:28-29 there is this promise about the Spirit, that He will be poured out on all people. It was through this same Holy Spirit that God raised Jesus from the dead, and now He dwells in us (Romans 8:11). The Holy Spirit is one, and He has always been the same. The way He works with people has appeared different at different times, but His heart has never changed.

column4: In John 20, after His resurrection, Jesus appears to His disciples in the middle of a locked room and breathes on them saying ‘*Receive the Holy Spirit*’ (John 20:22). The theology is somewhat debated on precisely what occurred at that moment, but most Pentecostal interpretations view this as the disciples receiving the Spirit of God inside them, signifying the new birth, being born-again. This was not, however when they received the Spirit of God upon them, empowering them with boldness for ministry. This was when they received the Holy Spirit within them, allowing them to abide and commune with God. This will be discussed at greater depth later in this chapter as well as the chapters on sanctification and baptism.
column5: In John 20, after the resurrection, Jesus appeared to His disciples in the middle of a locked room and breathed on them and said, 'Receive the Holy Spirit' (John 20:22). That was the time when they received the Holy Spirit within, enabling them to abide with God and have fellowship with Him. This will be discussed in greater depth later in this chapter and in the chapters on sanctification and baptism.

column4: The Holy Spirit is first and foremost, from and of God. The scriptures refer to the Spirit as the Spirit of God, or the Spirit of the Lord, or the Spirit of Christ, while these highlight different aspects, they are all one in the same. The Holy Spirit, being fully God, is also eternal and is holy (blameless, innocent, pure, not profane). Some translations refer to the Holy Spirit as the Holy Ghost.
column5: The Holy Spirit is, above all, of God and belongs to God. The Scriptures call the Spirit the Spirit of God, or the Spirit of the Lord, or the Spirit of Christ; although these highlight different aspects, they are all the same. The Holy Spirit, since he is fully God, is also eternal and holy (blameless, innocent, pure, undefiled). Some translations also call the Holy Spirit the Holy Ghost.

column4: The word spirit in Greek is ***Pneuma** (NYOO-mah -* **G4151***),* it means breath, or wind. The Hebrew word for spirit means the same. Breath is significant as we need it in constant supply to live. It was God's breath that He blew into Adam to bring Him to life, likewise it was Jesus' breath that He breathed last before He died on the cross. Without breath there is no life. Breath like wind can be felt and experienced but are not as easily observed as other ‘elements’ water, fire, earth.
column5: In Greek, the word for Spirit is ***Pneuma** (NYOO-mah -* **G4151***),* which means breath, or wind. In Hebrew, the word for spirit carries the same meaning. Breath is important because we need it continually to live. It was God’s breath that he breathed into Adam and gave him life, and likewise it was Jesus’ own breath that he drew one last time before he died on the cross. Without breath there is no life. Breath, like wind, can be felt and experienced, but it is not as easily observed as the other ‘elements’—water, fire, earth.

column4: ## Building a Relationship with the Holy Spirit
column5: ## Establishing a Relationship with the Holy Spirit

column4: Every relationship takes time and experience to develop deeply. The Holy Spirit is our advocate, our comforter, our helper, and our guide. He empowers us and sanctifies us.
column5: Every relationship requires time and experience to deepen. The Holy Spirit is our advocate, our comforter, our helper, and our guide. He empowers us and sanctifies us.

column4: Start to think of the Holy Spirit as you would a person. In our relationship we can both work to build it or do things that weaken our relationship. He can be ignored, He can be quenched, He can be blasphemed, or He can be listened to, honored, and obeyed.
column5: Begin to think about the Holy Spirit the way you think about a person. In a relationship, both parties can either work to strengthen it or do things that weaken it. He can be ignored, quenched, insulted, or he can be listened to, honored, and obeyed.

column4: Don’t ignore the voice of the Holy Spirit. He is always speaking to us and the church. If you don’t yet know how to distinguish the voice of the Holy Spirit, it takes time, willingness, and effort (like all healthy and beneficial relationships). But don’t worry, you already have built into you all the necessary parts needed to start to develop a personal relationship with the Holy Spirit.
column5: Do not ignore the voice of the Holy Spirit. He is always speaking to us and to the Church. If you do not yet know how to recognize the voice of the Holy Spirit, it takes time, desire, and effort (as in every healthy and fruitful relationship). But don’t worry, you already have within you everything necessary to begin establishing a personal relationship with the Holy Spirit.

column4: The quickest and most reliable ways to build an effective relationship with the Holy Spirit is to
column5: The quickest and most reliable ways to establish an effective relationship with the Holy Spirit are to

column4: 1.  Call out to Him **individually** in prayer, pause and wait for Him to speak.
column5: 1.  Call out to him **individually** in prayer, pause, and wait for him to speak.

column4: 2.  Call out to Him as part of a **group** of people who know Him (the church), pause, and wait for Him to speak.
column5: 2.  With a **group** of people who know him (the Church), call out to him, pause, and wait for him to speak.

column4: I use the phrase ‘call out’ to mean literally, with your mouth, or however you speak (with your hands if you cannot speak aloud with your mouth). Why speak? A few reasons:
column5: By the term 'call out' I mean literally speaking with your mouth, or however you speak (if you cannot speak aloud with your mouth, then with your hands). Why speak? A few reasons:

column4: 1.  We are speaking spirits made in God's image. God speaks, and so do we.
column5: 1.  We are speaking spirits made in the image of God. God speaks, and so do we.

column4: 2.  We use speaking as the primary way to communicate. You can also write down what you want to say (journaling) and speak it aloud.
column5: 2.  We primarily use speech for communication. You can also write what you want to say (journaling) and speak it out loud.

column4: 3.  Speaking is an intentional act, and indicates to the party you are talking to, that you’d like to engage them in a conversation.
column5: 3.  Speaking is an intentional act, and it signals to the party you are addressing that you want to engage in conversation with them.

column4: #### What should you say?
column5: #### What should you say?

column4: If you’ve never talked to God, try introducing yourself. Sure, it will feel a bit weird, but that discomfort is okay and temporary. Along with introducing yourself, tell God that you want to talk to Him and that you want Him to talk back to you.
column5: If you have never spoken to God, try introducing yourself. Certainly, it will feel a bit strange, but that discomfort is okay and temporary. Along with your introduction, tell God that you want to talk with him and that you want him to answer you.

column4: Consider asking Him a question. It doesn’t have to be a deep theological question; it can start simple. Can you show me Your love for me? Why do I have a certain feeling? What would You like to tell me?
column5: Consider asking him a question. It does not have to be a deep theological question; it can start simple. Can you show me your love for me? Why do I feel a certain way? What would you like to tell me?

column4: #### Then what?
column5: #### Then what?

column4: Well in all effective relationships you speak for a bit, then you pause and listen. God will speak.
column5: Well, in every effective relationship you speak for a while, then pause and listen. God will speak.

column4: God speaks in many ways, but He wants to do it personally, and internally. It will likely not be an audible voice (like if your best friend was to say your name aloud) but it will be an internal voice that speaks to your heart and mind. Elijah refers to this as the ‘still small voice’ (1 Kings 19:11-13).
column5: God speaks in many ways, but he wants to do this personally and internally. It will probably not be an audible voice (like your best friend calling your name out loud) but an inner voice that speaks to your heart and mind. Elijah calls it a 'still small voice' (1 Kings 19:11-13).

column4: The most common ways that I've personally witnessed God talk to people, and I've been blessed to help dozens of people learn how to talk to God directly, is some combination of the following:
column5: The ways I have personally most commonly seen God speak to people, and I have been blessed to help dozens of people learn to speak directly with God, tend to be some combination of the following:

column4: - A knowing - the person talking to God gets an immediate understanding that helps them.
column5: - An insight - the person who is speaking with God immediately receives understanding that helps them.

column4: - A picture - also known in the scriptures as a vision or a dream (a vision is when you are awake, a dream is when you are asleep), God will give you a picture in your mind. Perhaps it’s a memory, or place you’ve been or know? Explore the picture, what do you see? What do you feel as a result? What’s happening?
column5: - An image - which is also called a vision or a dream in the Scriptures (a vision when you are awake, a dream when you are asleep); God will give you an image in your mind. Perhaps it is a memory, or a place you have been or that you know? Explore the image; what do you see? As a result, what do you feel? What is happening?

column4: - An inner voice - like an audible voice, but one that only you can hear, and spoken into your heart and mind.
column5: - An inner voice - like an audible voice, but one that only you can hear, and that is spoken in your heart and mind.

column4: #### What will God say?
column5: #### What will God say?

column4: Not sure! But that’s the fun in it. I can say that He is NOT the spirit of fear, but of perfect love and that it will never violate the teaching of the scriptures. E.g., God will never tell you to commit an extra-marital affair.
column5: Not sure! But that’s the fun of it. I can say that it is not a spirit of fear but of perfect love, and it will never contradict the teaching of Scripture. For example, God will never tell you to have an extramarital affair.

column4: Now what?
column5: Now what?

column4: Keep the dialogue going! It’s really that simple.
column5: Keep the conversation going! It really is that simple.

column4: The Holy Spirit is the Helper. The Helper helps us! The work goes much more smoothly if we have a shared language, and relationship with Him. Can you imagine trying to work with someone in your job if you had no relationship, did not speak the same language, and couldn't communicate?!
column5: The Holy Spirit is the Helper. The Helper helps us! If there is a common language and relationship between us and Him, the work goes much more smoothly. Can you imagine trying to work at your job with someone with whom you have no relationship, who does not speak your language, and with whom you cannot communicate?!

column4: We serve a God who wants to communicate with us. Jesus said that His sheep know His voice (John 10:27), we have built into us all already the natural abilities we need, but we may lack experienced proficiency.
column5: We serve a God who wants to communicate with us. Jesus said that His sheep know His voice (John 10:27), the innate abilities we need have already been placed in all of us, but we may lack practiced skill.

column4: Speaking from personal experience, a personal and active relationship with the Holy Spirit is one of the best things about being a Christian. His presence brings us peace, comfort, and direction, but only if you know how to seek, listen, and obey Him.
column5: In my personal experience, a personal and active relationship with the Holy Spirit is one of the best things about being a Christian. His presence gives us peace, comfort, and guidance, but only when you know how to seek Him, listen, and obey Him.

column4: Develop a sensitivity with the Holy Spirit. Like many married people over time, you can communicate with your spouse in a unique way and sometimes just through a look. The look alone tells you everything you need to know about what just happened and what's going to happen. Build that type of sensitivity and familiarity with the Holy Spirit. Include Him in your whole life, this is a wonderful part of your relationship with Him that will provide so much depth and richness to your walk of faith.
column5: Cultivate sensitivity to the Holy Spirit. As many married people, over time, can communicate with their spouse in a unique way, and sometimes with just a glance. That look alone tells you everything that just happened and what is about to happen. Develop that same kind of sensitivity and familiarity with the Holy Spirit. Involve Him in your whole life; this is a wonderful aspect of your relationship with Him that will add much depth and richness to your walk of faith.

column4: The Holy Spirit has come to lead us and guide us, to empower us to be God’s people, and to see the people of the Earth radically transformed, delivered from the kingdom of darkness into the kingdom of light. Getting to know him, building trust with Him is essential to everyday life and to accomplish the work that Jesus has for us to do.
column5: The Holy Spirit came to lead and guide us, to empower us to be God’s people, and so that we would see the people of the earth completely transformed and freed from the kingdom of darkness into the kingdom of light. Knowing Him and building trust in Him is essential for everyday life and for completing the work Jesus has assigned us to do.
